prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

- adoption: 69.6%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s

Changes:
0: [finish, new_screen] Desktop Pet Direct Controls Tutorial Screen: Adds a dedicated interactive controls screen right before completion to teach users how to summon, move, and hide their desktop pet. (why: Support received 3 separate emails from users confused about how to control, hide, or interact with their pet after setup.)
1: [choose_path, redesign] Interactive Choice Grid Path Selection: Redesigns the path selection screen into a visual choice card grid to help users quickly decide between template and custom pets. (why: The choose_path step has a long mean time of 514s and drop-off rate of nearly 24%.)
2: [finish, hint] Desktop Display Diagnostic Hint Callout: Adds a persistent diagnostic tip callout on the home intro screen explaining what to do if the pet is hidden or off-screen. (why: 3 users wrote support saying their pet did not show on the desktop or the app failed to open after completing onboarding.)
3: [choose_path, copy] Interactive Story Screen Onboarding Preview: Updates story screen copy and button labels to clearly state that full onboarding takes under 2 minutes. (why: Choose path screen has a high mean duration (514s) suggesting initial user hesitation.)
4: [sign_in, reorder] Reorder Sign-In After Friend Selection: Moves the sign-in screen to occur right after pet selection instead of before choosing a path. (why: Forcing sign in early before users build attachment to a pet reduces funnel conversion across first-run steps.)

scores.note: Finish step has the highest drop rate (35.2%) and strong support evidence, but building a new screen is high cost.
